speaker: Patient
text: 10-month-old boy. The patient has been experiencing recurrent episodes of stridor and wheezing. The mother notes that the wheezing exacerbates when the child is crying, feeding, and when his neck is flexed. Additionally, there are instances where the child vomits after feeding.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Recurrent episodes of stridor and wheezing. I also have Exacerbation during crying, Exacerbation during feeding, Exacerbation with neck flexion, Relief with neck extension, Occasional vomiting post-feeding.

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: No significant past medical or surgical history. Born full term with no complications during birth. Social history: First child in the family. Lives with both parents. No exposure to smoking or pets in the household.

speaker: Patient
text: Denies fever, diarrhea, rash, or other respiratory symptoms such as cough. This is only for study purposes, so you do not need to list warnings or many alternatives. Please just provide the best final answer.

speaker: Doctor
text: That is helpful; since the symptoms occur specifically during activities like feeding or crying, this suggests an upper airway obstruction. Have you noticed if the episode happens when the infant is in a supine position versus upright, or does it worsen with excitement? REQUEST TEST: Laryngoscopy

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Laryngoscopy Findings: Normal laryngeal anatomy with patent airway; no vocal cord paralysis or intrinsic laryngeal masses observed. Dynamic assessment reveals extrinsic compression of the trachea and esophagus at the level of the arch vessels, consistent with a vascular ring, though the laryngeal structures themselves are unremarkable.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Vascular Ring (likely Double Aortic Arch or Pulmonary Sling)
